thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Potential cross-tenant header bleed detected in Dedicated GPU Pool us-west-2-pool-7 (dedicated-nexa). Alert ALERT-2026-03-15-0023. Suspect: X-Client-Meta header leaking on egress path.

maya.khan: Paging oncall. I see increased 5xxs and a small number of requests showing another tenant id in the X-Client-Meta value. Not sure if it's logging quirk or real leakage. 

devon.liu: On it. I'm looking at the egress proxy config for us-west-2-pool-7 now. Can anyone confirm customer impact — are we seeing payloads cross tenant boundaries?

nexa-support: Nexa Ops: we have a customer report — one of our app engineers saw an unexpected account_id in response headers for 3 requests. We quarantined the sessions. Happy to provide request IDs if helpful.

eli.nguyen: @devon can you run `grep -A3 "X-Client-Meta" /var/log/egress-proxy/us-west-2-pool-7.log | tail -n 50` and paste a sanitized snippet? Might be a header rewrite race.

devon.liu: Pasted snippet below (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T12:14:05Z] req_id=abc123 tenant=dedicated-nexa -> forwarded headers: {X-Client-Meta: "tenant:dedicated-nexa;session:..."}
[2026-03-15T12:14:06Z] req_id=abc124 tenant=dedicated-nexa -> forwarded headers: {X-Client-Meta: "tenant:acme-payments;session:..."}
```

maya.khan: OK that's not just logging. We have header from acme-payments showing up on nexA resources. Confirming cross-tenant header on egress path.

ops-oncall: Recommending immediate mitigation: 1) place us-west-2-pool-7 in drain, 2) isolate pool egress rules to deny external forwarding while we audit, 3) rotate session tokens for affected customers. Can we do a quick canary drain?

devon.liu: Draining pool: `redwood pool drain --pool us-west-2-pool-7 --mode canary --timeout 600s` — starting now. I'll also flip the egress proxy to strict header-scrub mode:
```
proxy.conf.header_scrub = true
proxy.conf.allow_listed_headers = ["Authorization","Content-Type"]
```

sre-bot: Action taken: pool drain initiated by devon.liu at 1774001400. Header-scrub toggled. Monitoring for new occurrences.

maya.khan: Nexa-support — please confirm whether they observed any sensitive payload in response body or only header anomalies.

nexa-support: Confirmed headers only, no PII in bodies per their checks. They flagged quickly, so scope appears limited to ~3 requests within a 5m window. They want SLA note and timeline.

security-engineer: Good catch. We'll need to rotate any customer-facing keys that could be tied to those sessions. Also start a routing config diff: `git diff origin/main..HEAD -- docs/egress` and run the audit script `tools/egress-routing-audit --pool us-west-2-pool-7 --check-headers`.

eli.nguyen: Running audit now. Early result: there was a transient nginx worker reuse bug combined with a header buffer reuse optimization after recent proxy patch (CL 3421). Repro steps in local env show header store reused across connections when `header_scrub=false`.

devon.liu: Patch found. Reverting CL 3421 on egress-proxy (rolling restart). Command: `deployctl revert --change 3421 --service egress-proxy --region us-west-2`. Rolling restart in progress.

sre-bot: Revert deploy triggered by devon.liu at 1774002100. Pool drain still in effect. No new cross-tenant headers observed in last 10m.

maya.khan: Customer impact summary for Nexa: 3 header-only anomalies, no body exposure, sessions possibly correlated. Nexa Ops requests immediate follow-up and postmortem. We've offered root-cause update and token rotation.

nexa-support: They appreciate the quick mitigation. Asking for ETA on full audit and whether we will notify other potentially affected customers.

security-engineer: Action items: 1) rotate session tokens and shorten TTL for any session IDs issued in the time window, 2) run full routing audit across dedicated pools created in last 30 days, 3) notify legal/compliance for notification guidance. I'll own 1 and 2.

ops-oncall: Handoff: I'm taking the follow-up until 1774003560; devon/eli please sync on postmortem notes. We'll schedule hotpostmortem 15:30 UTC. For now: pool remains draining, egress proxy patched back, header-scrub enforced cluster-wide.

maya.khan: Logging timeline + customer comms draft will go into #incidents-postmortems after hot call. Assigning postmortem owner: devon.liu.

devon.liu: I'll own the postmortem and remediation tickets. Will include reproducer, CL revert, and a config guard to prevent header reuse optimizations without explicit scrub.

sre-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED (initial mitigation in place). Escalation: postmortem required.

security-engineer: Follow-ups assigned: SE-1283 (rotate tokens), SE-1284 (egress audit), SRE-712 (guard in deploy pipeline).

maya.khan: Thanks team. Nexa wants a 1:1 update in 2 hours. ops-oncall, please lead the handoff to support and ensure customer update happens.

ops-oncall: Confirmed. Handoff done at 1774003560. I'll post final incident notes shortly. :white_check_mark:
